beats.text: More than half of all countries earn most of their export money from raw materials.
Oil, metals, crops. Dug up or grown, then sold.
Each country rises when we show its number one export.
Oil and coal: from Norway to Nigeria to Saudi Arabia.
Gold, copper and other metals: much of Africa and the Andes.
Crops: coffee in Ethiopia, cocoa in Ivory Coast, soy in Brazil.
Cars, phones and medicine: mostly Europe and East Asia.
Most of the world still drills, digs or grows. It's

sources: UNCTAD (2023), The State of Commodity Dependence 2023 – 101 of 191 UNCTAD member states (52.9 %) were commodity-dependent in 2019–2021 (commodities > 60 % of merchandise export value); 95 of 142 developing countries (66.9 %).

Map: each country's single top export product, 2018, CEPII (BACI) via Visual Capitalist, 'Mapped: The Top Export in Every Country'; India, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Timor-Leste added as petroleum (OEC 2018). Grouped by us into oil & coal / metals / crops & food / manufactured goods. Countries without data stay flat.
